name: Petroglyphs along the Bangucheon Stream
description: Along the Bangucheon Stream near Ulsan, on South Korea's southeast coast, cliff faces hold thousands of years of carvings at two sites, Daegok-ri and Cheonjeon-ri. The best known is the Bangudae panel, about 8 metres wide, where lively scenes of whales, hunters and land animals were scratched into the rock. People kept adding to it from around 5000 BCE to the 9th century CE.
